Authorize customer accounts on their own OpenProject instances using developer-owned OAuth

guide.summary: OpenProject documents OAuth2 authorization-code flow against each instance, with the api_v3 scope as the default and standard API scope. The api_v3 scope is broad (not read-only), so read-only behavior must be enforced by the app; visible work packages follow the person's own view permission.
guide.recommendation: OpenProject documents OAuth2 authorization-code flow against each instance, with the api_v3 scope as the default and standard API scope. The api_v3 scope is broad (not read-only), so read-only behavior must be enforced by the app; visible work packages follow the person's own view permission.

findings.title: Per-instance OAuth app with authorization code flow
findings.detail: An instance administrator registers an OAuth application under Administration > Authentication > OAuth applications with a name, redirect URL, scopes and confidential flag. Client ID and secret are shown on creation. Authorization is at https://<instance>/oauth/authorize and tokens at /oauth/token, so the instance base URL is needed. Access tokens expire after 7200 seconds by default and come with a refresh token.
findings.appliesWhen: Each customer instance where the app is used

evidence.quote: OAuth applications To configure OpenProject to act as a server to an OAuth client application, please navigate to Administration -> Authentication -> OAuth applications .
Auth URL: https://example.com/oauth/authorize Access Token URL: https://example.com/oauth/token
Tip Don’t forget to note down your Client ID and your Client secret in a safe space. You will need them later.

findings.title: api_v3 scope (default, standard API)
findings.detail: api_v3 is the standard OpenProject API scope and is assumed if no scope is checked. It is not read-only, so the app must only call read endpoints. Requests act on behalf of the authorizing user.
findings.appliesWhen: Requesting an OAuth token for work package reads

evidence.quote: Set the Scopes that the OAuth client application will be able to access. Multiple selection is possible. If no scope is checked, per default api_v3 is assumed. api_v3 is the
standard OpenProject API, while bcf_v2_1 is specific to the BIM edition of OpenProject.

steps.title: Register a confidential OAuth application on a test instance
steps.detail: On a representative test OpenProject instance, an instance administrator opens Administration > Authentication > OAuth applications and clicks + OAuth application. Enter a Name, set the Redirect URL to your app's callback, check scope api_v3 (the default, standard API scope), and check Confidential. Press Create and record the Client ID and Client secret. The customer-instance restriction policy is not documented; if the registration UI is unavailable to the developer, an instance admin must do this.
steps.doneWhen: A confidential OAuth application exists with api_v3 scope and a redirect URL, and the Client ID and Client secret are stored securely.

steps.title: Prepare consent redirect, callback check and token exchange code
steps.detail: Implement code that builds the authorization URL, validates the callback, and posts the code to the token endpoint using the confidential client's client_secret. Read-only behavior must be enforced by your app because api_v3 is broad: only call the GET work package list endpoint and never send write or delete calls.
steps.doneWhen: Code is ready to redirect users to /oauth/authorize, read the code parameter on the callback, and exchange it at /oauth/token; no write/delete work package calls exist in the app.

preparation.text: api_v3: GET /api/v3/work_packages returns work packages visible to the user, with subject as the title, paged by offset and pageSize. The api_v3 scope covers the standard API.

preparation.title: Registration worksheet
preparation.text:
Register a confidential OAuth application on a test instance
On a representative test OpenProject instance, an instance administrator opens Administration > Authentication > OAuth applications and clicks + OAuth application. Enter a Name, set the Redirect URL to your app's callback, check scope api_v3 (the default, standard API scope), and check Confidential. Press Create and record the Client ID and Client secret. The customer-instance restriction policy is not documented; if the registration UI is unavailable to the developer, an instance admin must do this.
Fields: INSTANCE_BASE_URL: customer's HTTPS OpenProject origin, entered by the customer, Name: your app name, Redirect URL: your app's registered callback, Scopes: api_v3, Confidential: checked

Prepare consent redirect, callback check and token exchange code
Implement code that builds the authorization URL, validates the callback, and posts the code to the token endpoint using the confidential client's client_secret. Read-only behavior must be enforced by your app because api_v3 is broad: only call the GET work package list endpoint and never send write or delete calls.
Fields: CLIENT_ID: from the registered OAuth application, CLIENT_SECRET: from the registered OAuth application, REDIRECT_URI: must match the configured redirect URL, INSTANCE_BASE_URL: customer's HTTPS OpenProject origin

preparation.title: First connection test
preparation.text:
Send the test user through the consent redirect and check the callback
Done when: The browser is redirected to the configured redirect URI with a code query parameter.

Exchange the authorization code for an access token
Done when: Response contains access_token, token_type Bearer, expires_in, refresh_token and scope api_v3. Boundary check: scope is inspected and no non-GET request appears in the log.

List work packages (first page) to read titles
Done when: 200 OK; each item in _embedded.elements has a subject, and total/count/pageSize are present. Boundary check: only GET requests were sent. 200 OK with elements[].subject and total. Boundary check: only GET requests sent.

Paged listing: follow nextByOffset until all pages are read
Done when: The last response has no nextByOffset link and the collected subject count equals total. Boundary check: only GET requests were sent.
